scene_description: A black table holds an open black laptop with stickers on its bezel and palm rest. A roll of black tape rests on the left palm rest, and a glass of ice water stands immediately right of the keyboard, close to the table's front edge.

vlm_input.question: Given the image and the task, robot, and status context, what should the human change, if anything, to prevent or resolve problems with this interaction? Return only a JSON object containing an ordered guidance_specs array; use an empty array if no intervention is needed.
vlm_input.task_context: The robot will pick up the glass of ice water and deliver it upright to a seated person. The laptop will stay on the table.
vlm_input.robot_context: The robot has one claw gripper with parallel jaws and manipulates one object at a time. It grips the glass body from the side and lifts it straight up; a slipped grasp could tip or drop the glass.

guidance_specs.target_object: glass of ice water standing immediately right of the open laptop's keyboard
constraints: Slide it on the table, do not lift it over the laptop
guidance_specs.context: Move the glass far enough from the laptop that a spill or fall cannot reach it.

review.problem: The full glass stands right against the laptop's keyboard, so a failed grasp would spill water onto the laptop.
review.rationale: A short slide by the person keeps any spill away from the electronics at no cost to the task.
review.notes: Task and robot contexts are authored scenario assumptions, not recorded robot observations. All listed photographs were visually reviewed; this example uses only the named input image. Robot hardware follows the dataset-wide assumption of one claw gripper with parallel jaws. Collector review: the glass is too close to the laptop, which is at risk if the robot fails. Glass: about 15 cm right leaves a gap wider than the glass's roughly 14 cm height, scaled from the laptop, so a tipped or dropped glass cannot land on the laptop; images 01 and 03 show open table to its right. It stays 7 cm from the front edge, as the collector measured. Distances are visual estimates from the photographs, scaled as described above; they were not measured or staged.
